import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

If you're about to change substrate admission/revocation, or a security review flags
something here as a "gap," read this first — several of these are **intentional** trust-model
decisions, not bugs.

## Two flavors of revocation (both enforced)

1. **Self-revocation** (`papercusp-substrate-revocation-v1-2026-06-01`). A contributor revokes
   their OWN device key (lost/rotated device). Mechanism: the device pubkey is added to that
   contributor's own `revoked_pubkeys` (a `TEXT[]` on `harness_shared.contributors`,
   replicated via the substrate). Trigger: `revokeSelfDevice` /
   `POST /api/admin/substrate/revoke-self-device` / the `substrate:revoke_self_device` MCP tool
   — guarded by `not_your_key` (you can only revoke keys in your OWN `device_attestations`).
   Enforcement: `boot.ts` seeds the admission `revoked` Set from `loadRevokedPubkeys` at startup
   (unconditional, fail-open) AND refreshes it inside every `mergeNow`.

2. **Owner-revocation** (`papercusp-substrate-revocation-v2-owner-2026-06-01`, Component A —
   PASSIVE detection; plus Component B, now BUILT with a different design than originally
   planned, see below). Kicking out a different contributor (a bad actor).
   - **Component A (passive, unchanged):** a repo admin **deletes the contributor's `user/<id>`
     branch** (the channel-2 artifact) directly on GitHub. Enforcement: `boot.ts` periodically
     **re-verifies admitted peers' channel-2** (throttled inside `mergeNow`, default ~15 min) and
     drops any whose binding conclusively `fail`s. This drop does **not** blocklist the pubkey
     (see below).
   - **Component B (active, `substrate:revoke_contributor` — `non-collaborator-join-fork-pr
     -2026-06-02` D-001, supersedes the old branch-delete design):** an in-app OWNER trigger.
     **The original "delete the `user/<id>` branch via the GitHub API" design was dropped before
     shipping** — it would have been a silent no-op, because admission moved to being gated on
     the contributor's attestation **gist** (`read-admission` → `verifyAttestation`), not a repo
     branch, and an admin can't delete another user's gist. The shipped design instead: the owner
     (gated on holding a GitHub token with **repo-admin** on the shared repo) adds the target's
     device pubkeys directly to the **owner's own** contributor-row `revoked_pubkeys` and
     publishes it — the same blocklist self-revocation uses (`revoke-contributor.ts`
     `revokeContributorViaGithub`). Every peer's `read-admission` union honors it on the next
     re-verify. A **Pot-scope** variant (`shared-pot-federation-2026-06-08` P-006,
     `pot-revoke-contributor.ts` `revokeHiveContributor`) revokes the contributor from a WHOLE
     Pot's federation (every member harness) in one call — its authority is **holding the
     Pot's private key**, not GitHub repo-admin (a Pot may be repo-less); see the authority
     section below.

<Aside type="caution" title="The gap that motivated rev-v2">
Model B verified a peer's channel-2 binding ONCE at admission and re-checked only PENDING
peers. An already-**admitted** peer was NEVER re-verified — so a deleted GitHub binding was
not noticed. If you see admission logic that only checks at admit-time, that gap is back.
</Aside>

## Why GitHub-anchored authority (not a papercusp owner gate)

Deliberate, consistent with `papercusp-trust-model-2026-05-31` + the **no-collaborator-gate**
decision + Phase-1b §8 / D-009: **GitHub is the real authority** for the thing that matters
(merging code); peer-synced state is **advisory**. An owner-signed revocation list was
considered and rejected — it reintroduces exactly the papercusp-side authority gate that
decision avoided, and the P-068 "owner" is only *provisional*/contestable. Re-verifying
channel-2 is **not** a collaborator gate; it re-applies the *same* check admission already
requires, just periodically.

**Update:** `substrate:revoke_contributor` (Component B, above) DOES now gate its harness-scope
action on a papercusp-side check — but it's still anchored in GitHub, not a papercusp-native
owner: the gate is "does the caller's GitHub token have **repo-admin** on the shared repo,"
checked live via `octokit.repos.get(...).permissions.admin`, the same authority Component A's
branch-delete always assumed. The **Pot-scope** variant is the one genuine departure: its
authority is **holding the Pot's private key** (a Pot can be repo-less), not a GitHub
permission at all — a deliberate, narrower keypair-native authority for the Pot-wide case.

## Intentional decisions a reviewer will want to "fix" (don't, without re-deciding the posture)

- **Fail-OPEN on a revocation/re-verify LOAD failure** (rev-v1 D-006, rev-v2 D-004). If the PG
  read or the GitHub API fails, admission continues WITHOUT the (new) revocation rather than
  evicting peers. Rationale: advisory substrate + GitHub-is-authority → a transient blip must
  not self-inflict a federation outage. It's **visible** (`merge_error`/`announce_error`
  events) and **self-healing** (re-checked next cycle). A channel-2-`fail` (conclusive) DOES
  drop; only transient (`pending`/api-down) keeps. Fail-secure (evict-on-failure) is the wrong
  trade here.
- **A channel-2-fail drop does NOT blocklist the pubkey.** A re-published binding is
  re-admitted by normal admission; a still-deleted binding is rejected (`binding_invalid`) —
  no flap. (Self-revocation DOES persist via `revoked_pubkeys` — that's the difference.)
- **Revocation is non-retroactive.** Ops a peer already merged remain (advisory; GitHub is
  authority). True cryptographic removal isn't a goal.

## Not built (intentional)

- **Multi-device per login** — see `phase1b-federation-limitations`.

## Built since this doc was first written (2026-07-03 update)

- **Rev-v2 Component B is now BUILT** (`substrate:revoke_contributor`, see above) — but with a
  *different* design than the branch-delete this doc originally described as "not built." The
  branch-delete trigger was dropped before shipping (it would have been a no-op once admission
  moved to gist-based attestation); the shipped trigger blocklists the target's pubkeys directly.
- **Un-revoke / re-instate is now PARTIALLY built** (`WI-193` "G8" fix in `boot.ts`
  `applyRevocationRefresh`) — this doc previously said it was YAGNI/append-only; that is no
  longer accurate for the *published-list* path. Any pubkey whose provenance is
  refresh-sourced (`revokedViaRefresh` — seeded at startup from `loadRevokedPubkeys`, or added
  by a later `applyRevocationRefresh` cycle) is **removed from `revoked`** the moment it
  disappears from the freshly-loaded published `revoked_pubkeys` set, re-admitting it on its
  next announce (a `peer_unrevoked` boot-history event records it). This can never silently
  undo an explicit **live** `revoke()` call (self-revoke or owner-revoke via the tools above) —
  `revoke()` evicts the pubkey from `revokedViaRefresh` too, so an explicit in-process
  revocation stays blocked for the life of that boot regardless of the published list. There is
  still no dedicated "un-revoke" MCP tool; the only way to un-revoke today is to edit the
  pubkey out of the relevant contributor row's `revoked_pubkeys` column directly (and, for a
  pubkey revoked live in the current process, restart the boot so the seed no longer includes
  it).
